name: XOR Encoding
description: XORs consecutive values to produce differences. Effective for time-series with small changes between values.

name: Delta Encoding (DIFF)
description: Simple first-order predictor that computes differences between consecutive values (also called difference sequence). Effective for monotonic or slowly varying data. A sign-magnitude conversion is often used on the output to produce more leading-zero bits for a modest extra compression gain in subsequent stages. This is equivalent to the 1D lorenzo predictor.

name: Lorenzo Predictor
description: Linear predictor that estimates data values based on neighboring values in 1D, 2D, or 3D grids. Uses weighted sum of adjacent values to predict current value, creating residuals for subsequent encoding. Includes variants: mean-integrated, tiled, and second-order.

papers.title: Out-of-core compression and decompression of large n-dimensional scalar fields
papers.authors: L. Ibarria, P. Lindstrom, J. Rossignac and A. Szymczak
papers.note: Original Lorenzo predictor paper and formulation

papers.title: Significantly Improving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data Sets Based on Multidimensional Prediction and Error-Controlled Quantization
papers.authors: D. Tao, S. Di, Z. Chen and F. Cappello
papers.note: SZ 1.4 algorithm - Lorenzo predictor in SZ

name: Curve Fitting / Regression
description: Fits a polynomial (flat/linear/quadratic/cubic) to each data block via regression, then predicts every point in the block from that one fit. More expressive than Lorenzo for smooth trends and gradients, at higher computational cost. Block size and polynomial order can be fixed or adaptively selected per block.
features: Block-based operation with adaptive block sizing

papers.title: Fast Error-Bounded Lossy HPC Data Compression with SZ
Significantly Improving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data Sets Based on Multidimensional Prediction and Error-Controlled Quantization
papers.authors: Tao D., Di S., Chen Z., Cappello F.
papers.note: Introduces polynomial regression predictors as extension to Lorenzo

name: Interpolation
description: Predicts values between known data points using smooth polynomial curves. There are linear, cubic, and multi-level (hierarchical resolution) variants. Cubic B-splines use piecewise parametric polynomial curves of degree 3, producing smooth second-order differentiable curves at knot locations - particularly effective on sorted monotonic data.

papers.title: Interpolation Methods
papers.note: Standard prediction techniques including spline and multi-level variants

papers.title: ISABELA for Effective In Situ Compression of Scientific Data
papers.authors: S. Lakshminarasimhan, N. Shah, S. Ethier, S-H. Ku, C.S Chang, S. Klasky, R. Latham, R. Ross, N.F. Samatova
papers.note: Cubic B-splines curve fitting for compression

name: Neural Network Prediction
description: Uses trained neural networks to predict data values. Learns complex patterns from training data for sophisticated prediction.

name: Downsampling / Pooling
description: Reduces resolution by aggregating blocks of values. Variants include average pooling, max pooling, selective (sparsity-aware), and strided downsampling. Reconstructs via interpolation.
features: Common in neural networks and image processing

name: Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT)
description: Frequency-domain transform that represents data as sum of cosine waves. Concentrates energy in low-frequency coefficients, enabling effective compression of smooth data. ZFP uses a near-orthogonal transform in this family. Used in image and video compression (JPEG, MPEG).

papers.title: A Fast Cosine Transform in One and Two Dimensions

name: Wavelet Transform
description: Multi-resolution transform that decomposes data into frequency subbands at different scales. Enables progressive compression and good for non-stationary signals. Used as the decorrelating transform in SPERR.

papers.title: A theory for multiresolution signal decomposition: the wavelet representation

name: SVD / Tensor Decomposition
description: Factorizes a matrix into singular values and vectors via singular value decomposition (SVD); for multi-dimensional (tensor) data, the Tucker decomposition generalizes SVD to higher-order arrays, factorizing the tensor into a small core tensor plus one factor matrix per dimension. The factorization itself is exact when all components are retained. Compression is achieved by retaining only the dominant components (rank truncation), a downstream/config-level choice rather than an inherent part of the decomposition.
features: Rank reduction via dominant singular values
Tucker/HOSVD generalizes SVD to N-D tensors
Good for smooth, structured multi-dimensional data

papers.title: Singular value decomposition and least squares solutions
papers.authors: G. H. Golub and C. Reinsch
papers.note: Widely used SVD algorithm and numerical method

papers.title: A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition
papers.authors: L. De Lathauwer, B. De Moor, J. Vandewalle
papers.note: Foundational HOSVD paper — Tucker/HOSVD generalization of SVD to tensors

verification.notes: renamed from tucker-decomposition and generalized to SVD, 2026-07-05; TZ compressor citation pending (preprint)

name: Multilevel Decomposition
description: Hierarchical decomposition based on multigrid methods that represents data at multiple levels of resolution. Creates a hierarchy of coefficients where each level captures different scales of variation in the data. Used in MGARD (its flagship component) for adaptive reduction with error control: the multilevel structure enables error bounds in the L-infinity or L2 norm and supports progressive, adaptable retrieval at multiple resolution levels. Works best on smooth continuous fields such as PDE solutions, where it delivers strong rate-distortion performance.
features: Supports multi-dimensional, single-dimensional, or hybrid modes

papers.title: MGARD+: Optimizing Multilevel Methods for Error-bounded Scientific Data Reduction
Multilevel Techniques for Compression and Reduction of Scientific Data
papers.note: Thesis on multilevel methods for scientific data compression

name: Bit Truncation
description: Removes least significant bits from floating-point mantissa. Simple lossy quantization by dropping precision bits.

name: Bit Grooming
description: Bitwise quantization that zeroes least-significant bits in floating-point mantissa to improve compressibility while preserving significant digits (NSD mode).

papers.title: Bit Grooming: Statistically accurate precision-preserving quantization with compression

name: Error-Bounded Quantizer
description: Maps each value to an integer code under a user-chosen error bound — the core lossy step in prediction-based compressors. Supports multiple error-bound modes (ABS, NOA, REL, pseudo-REL) that trade accuracy against how the bound scales with the data.
features: Multiple error modes: ABS, NOA, REL, pseudo-REL
Per-point error guaranteed under the chosen bound
Integer codes suited to entropy coding downstream
Range-relative (NOA) adapts the bound to the data span

name: Linear Quantization
description: Uniform quantization that divides value range into equal-sized bins. Maps continuous values to discrete levels with predictable error bounds and compression ratios.

papers.title: Quantization
papers.note: Standard technique in signal processing literature

name: Vector Quantization
description: Quantizes vectors rather than scalars. Uses codebook of representative vectors for block-based compression.

name: Twos-Complement to Magnitude-Sign (TCMS)
description: Converts each value from twos-complement to magnitude-sign representation. Produces more leading zero bits, improving compressibility for subsequent stages.

name: Zigzag Encoding
description: Maps a signed integer to an unsigned integer by doubling the absolute value and subtracting 1 when the original value was negative. Small-magnitude values, positive or negative, map to small unsigned codes. This produces very similar output to TCMS (identical for positive values, slightly different for negative values).
features: Doubles magnitude, interleaves sign into the low bit
Small |n| maps to a small unsigned code regardless of sign

papers.title: Making All Your Integers Positive with Zigzag Encoding
papers.note: Blog post detailing the zigzag encoding technique.

verification.notes: New module split from zigzag-ordering, 2026-07-07. FZGM's ZigzagStage was previously misassigned to zigzag-ordering (a distinct scan-order technique); corrected to this module.

name: Negabinary Signed-to-Unsigned Map
description: Element-wise negabinary (base −2) representation: maps signed integers to an unsigned base-(−2) encoding. Like TCMS and zigzag's value-mapping sense, this reshapes a signed residual stream so small-magnitude values (positive or negative) produce more high-order zero/repeated bits.

verification.notes: generalized from FZGM implementation card; negabinary origin paper is a best-effort, unverified citation

name: IEEE-754 Field Reorder
description: De-biases the IEEE-754 floating-point exponent and reorders the sign/exponent/fraction fields into a fixed byte layout, grouping similar field types together across values to improve downstream compressibility. Two field orders are used in practice: exponent-fraction-sign (EFS) and exponent-sign-fraction (ESF); the exponent de-biasing is identical, only the byte order of the reassembled fields differs.
features: Field reordering variants: EFS and ESF byte layouts
Groups similar field types for better downstream entropy coding

name: Fixed-Point Conversion
description: Converts floating-point values to a fixed-point integer representation (a deterministic ldexp-style scale) for bit-exact, platform-independent reproducibility. Unlike error-bound quantization, this is a lossless representation change within the chosen fixed-point range, not a binning step tied to an error tolerance.
features: No error bound involved -- exact within representable range

verification.notes: New module created 2026-07-13 from FZ Module Library's catalog (FixedPointQuantizer page); no exact prior Z-Hub module matched.

name: Logarithmic Scaling
description: Applies logarithmic scaling to compress dynamic range. Effective for data spanning multiple orders of magnitude.

name: Move-to-Front Transform
description: Maintains list of symbols and moves recently used symbols to front. Produces small values for repeated symbols, improving compression.
features: Produces small numbers for repeated access

name: Block-Floating-Point Transform
description: Represents a block of floating-point values with a single shared exponent and individual mantissas. Efficiently encodes zero blocks with a single bit. Reduces redundancy by factoring out the common exponent component across spatially correlated values.

name: Data Normalization
description: Scales data to standard range (e.g., [0,1] or [-1,1]). Improves compressibility and numerical stability.

name: Adaptive Data Mapping
description: Adaptive Data Mapping (ADM): partitions a stream into fixed-size blocks, computes a per-block center (e.g. the block mean), and remaps each element to a compact code relative to that center — shrinking a wide integer stream (e.g. u16/u32) into a narrow symbol domain (e.g. 8-bit) before entropy coding. The narrower, more concentrated symbol distribution compresses substantially better under a subsequent entropy coder (e.g. ANS/Huffman) than the raw wide-integer stream.
features: Remaps wide integer codes into a compact symbol domain

papers.title: MANS: Efficient and Portable ANS Encoding for Multi-Byte Integer Data on CPUs and GPUs
papers.note: ADM stage as preprocessing for ANS entropy coding

verification.notes: generalized from FZGM implementation card; MANS paper citation still pending (repo-level attribution only)

name: Bit Shuffle (Transpose)
description: Transposes bits across values by collecting most significant bits together, then second most significant bits, and so on. Improves compressibility when values share similar bit patterns.
features: Improves compressibility for correlated bit positions

name: Zigzag Ordering
description: Reorders multi-dimensional coefficients (typically from frequency transforms like DCT) in a zigzag pattern from low to high frequency. Creates roughly monotonically decreasing magnitude sequence, improving subsequent encoding efficiency. Not to be confused with zigzag encoding (see zigzag-encoding), a distinct, unrelated technique that shares only the name — it maps signed integers to unsigned integers rather than reordering coefficient positions.

papers.title: Fixed-Rate Compressed Floating-Point Arrays
papers.note: Zigzag ordering of DCT coefficients in ZFP

verification.notes: FZGM's ZigzagStage implementation entry moved to zigzag-encoding, 2026-07-07 (it was misassigned here — see that module's notes).

name: Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT)
description: Rearranges characters to group similar contexts together. Improves compressibility for subsequent encoding (used in bzip2).
features: Text-friendly but works on any data

papers.title: A Block-sorting Lossless Data Compression Algorithm

name: Tuple Shuffle
description: Rearranges k-tuples by grouping all first elements, then all second elements, etc. Benefits compression when values within the same dimension correlate more than across tuples.

name: Sorting
description: Pre-conditioning step that sorts data values in increasing order. Converts irregular spatial distributions into smooth monotonic curves, making subsequent curve fitting more accurate. Particularly effective for scientific data with high spatial irregularity.
features: Converts irregular data to monotonic curves

papers.title: ISABELA for Effective In Situ Compression of Scientific Data
papers.authors: S. Lakshminarasimhan, N. Shah, S. Ethier, S-H. Ku, C.S Chang, S. Klasky, R. Latham, R. Ross, N.F. Samatova

name: Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
description: Lossless compression that replaces sequences of repeated values with (value, count) pairs. Most effective for data with long runs of identical values.

name: Repeat/Zero Elimination
description: Builds a bitmap flagging which words match a target value, emits only the non-matching words, and recursively compresses the bitmap itself. The zero-specialized variant (RZE) targets exactly zero; the general variant (RRE) matches any repeated value (e.g. the previous word). Same bitmap-and-compact structure, different match criterion.
features: Effective for sparse or repetitive data

name: Bit Packing
description: Packs data values into smaller bit widths than their native representation, eliminating unused high-order bits. Reduces storage size for data with small dynamic range.

name: Bitplane Packing
description: Packs quantized integer values MSB-to-LSB into separate per-bit-significance streams (bitplanes), enabling progressive/refinable decoding -- higher-order planes can be decoded first for a coarse reconstruction, with lower-order planes added incrementally. Applies no compression by itself; downstream stages (RLE, entropy coding) exploit the resulting sparsity, especially in high-order planes.
features: No compression on its own -- reshapes data for downstream coders
Distinct from bit-packing's fixed-width repack and truncation's mantissa discard

papers.title: Progressive/Adaptable Retrieval via Multigrid Decomposition (PMGARD)
papers.note: Cited by FZ Module Library as relying on MSB-to-LSB bitplane order for progressive retrieval

verification.notes: New module created 2026-07-13 from FZ Module Library's catalog (BitplaneEncoder page); no exact prior Z-Hub module matched.

name: Compressed Leading-Zero Groups (CLOG)
description: Breaks data into subchunks and records the count of leading zero bits for each. Stores only the remaining significant bits, compressing values with many leading zeros. An adaptive variant additionally applies a TCMS (magnitude-sign) transform first to subchunks with no leading zeros, handling mixed bit patterns better than plain CLOG.
features: Efficient for values with common high-order bits

name: Dictionary Encoding
description: Maps frequently occurring patterns to short codes using a dictionary/codebook, exploiting repeated sequences rather than per-value statistics. Classic LZ78/LZW-style dictionary coding; related to but distinct from LZ77's sliding-window matching.

papers.title: Compression of Individual Sequences via Variable-Rate Coding

name: LZ77 (Lempel-Ziv 1977)
description: Dictionary-based compression using sliding window. Replaces repeated sequences with back-references. Used in gzip, DEFLATE, Zstandard.

papers.title: A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression

name: Huffman Encoding
description: Variable-length entropy coding algorithm that assigns shorter codes to more frequent symbols. Builds a binary tree based on symbol frequencies for optimal prefix coding. Limited by integer bit lengths.

papers.title: A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes

name: Arithmetic Coding
description: Entropy coding that represents entire message as single number in [0,1) interval. Achieves compression closer to theoretical entropy limit than Huffman coding.

papers.title: Arithmetic Coding for Data Compression
papers.authors: Witten I.H., Neal R.M., Cleary J.G.

name: Range Coding
description: Entropy coding similar to arithmetic coding but simpler. Maps input to subranges of [0,1) interval.

name: Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS)
description: Modern entropy coding combining speed of Huffman with compression of arithmetic coding. Used in Zstandard (FSE variant).

name: SPECK Coding
description: SPECK repeatedly tests large rectangular regions of wavelet coefficients for significance at descending bitplane thresholds, splitting only those regions that contain large values, and refining discovered coefficients progressively. Used as the coefficient coder in SPERR.

papers.authors: W. A. Pearlman and A. Islam
papers.note: Introduced as a low complexity option for JPEG2000

papers.title: Embedded image coding using zeroblocks of subband/wavelet coefficients and context modeling
papers.note: higher complexity variant of SPECK, called (embedded zero block coding (EZBC))

papers.title: Efficient, low-complexity image coding with a set-partitioning embedded block coder
papers.authors: W.A. Pearlman, A. Islam, N. Nagaraj, A. Said
